title: Complete summary – Digestive tract & abdomen
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture. 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Barium studies 🔁🔁

  • Indications: chronic conditions of the digestive tract, findings seen on other imaging, post-operative morphology/function, achalasia evaluation, chronic ulcer follow-up.
  • Contraindications: perforation (absolute → water-soluble iodine), acute inflammation (e.g. acute diverticulitis), suspected post-operative leak.
  • Vocabulary: addition image (niche) = ulcer; subtraction (filling defect, lacuna) = tumour.

Oesophagus 🔁🔁🔁

Achalasia (2022, 2023 and 2025)

  • Marked dilatation and elongation of the oesophagus, air-fluid level with barium sedimentation.
  • ABSENCE of the gastric air bubble ⚠
  • Bird's beak = SHORT, smooth, progressive (tapered) stenosis at the lower oesophageal sphincter. A long, irregular or shouldered stricture = cancer.

Benign vs malignant stricture

BenignMalignant
Axial (concentric), progressive narrowing, smooth edges, proximal dilatation depending on its ageEccentric, abrupt junction ("shoulders"), irregular edges, filling defects (lacunar images), semilunar contours

Stomach – gastric ulcer 🔁

  • Ulcer = addition image (niche), NOT subtraction ⚠
  • Benign signs: Hampton line (transparent line at the base), sharp protrusion beyond the contour of the lesser curvature, regular converging folds.
  • A contralateral incisura is not a malignancy sign.

Plain abdominal film 🔁

  • Intestinal occlusion = air-fluid (hydro-aeric) levels along the digestive tract.
  • Transparent crescent under the diaphragm = pneumoperitoneum; Rigler sign (both sides of the bowel wall) = perforation / pneumoperitoneum; apple core = colon carcinoma ⚠
  • Valvulae conniventes = small bowel (central); haustra = colon (peripheral).
  • Apple core on barium enema = colon carcinoma (annular stenosis with shoulders).

Small bowel – MR enterography

  • Loops must be distended and filled with fluid (oral mannitol/PEG) + antispasmodic; no air, no movement, not empty.

Liver 🔁🔁🔁

  • Increased echogenicity ("bright liver"): steatosis, fibrosis. Hypoechoic: acute hepatitis ("starry sky"), congestive hepatopathy. Polycystic = multiple anechoic cysts.
  • Haemangioma on US: typically HYPERECHOIC.
  • Most frequent malignant lesions in a non-cirrhotic liver: METASTASES. HCC → cirrhotic liver.
  • HCC surveillance in chronic hepatitis/cirrhosis: ultrasound every 6 months (± AFP).

CT patterns – liver tumours (2022, 2023, 2025)

  • i.v. contrast REQUIRED for characterisation; analysis of several phases gives the diagnosis. Lesions can be hypo-, iso- or hyperdense; small ones can be missed; they are NOT always seen only in the portal phase.
  • Peripheral globular (nodular) enhancement with centripetal progression → BENIGN (haemangioma).
  • Quick portal WASH-OUT → MALIGNANT (HCC: arterial wash-in, portal wash-out).
  • Intense arterial enhancement alone does NOT mean malignant (FNH, adenoma, flash-filling haemangioma) ⚠
  • Metastases: hypovascular in the portal phase. FNH: central scar. Cyst: never enhances.

Liver metastases – FALSE statements asked (old exam, 2022, 2025)

  • ✗ "They can never be cystic" – they CAN be cystic.
  • ✗ "They usually enhance markedly in the portal phase" – they usually wash out / are hypovascular.
  • True: usually multiple nodular lesions, similar size/pattern, specific behaviour on contrast CT/MRI, often shown by US.

Gadoxetic acid (Primovist) MRI

  • Indicated for: hepatocellular vs non-hepatocellular tumours, FNH characterisation, small metastases, biliary fistulas. NOT for detecting haemangiomas.

Biliary tract 🔁🔁

  • Normal values: intrahepatic ducts < 2 mm (thinner than the portal branch, often not seen); CBD at the hilum ≤ 7 mm; gallbladder transverse diameter up to ~4 cm (not 6); gallbladder wall ≤ 3–4 mm.
  • Gallstones are NOT always seen on native CT (only calcified ones; many are isodense).
  • Gallstones on US (screening method = US): hyperechoic, mobile, with a sharp posterior acoustic shadow; single or multiple; may fill the whole gallbladder or be impacted in the infundibulum. NOT transsonic with enhancement (= fluid).
  • Obstructive jaundice: caused by pancreatic head tumours, cholangiocarcinoma, stones. CBD stones: MRCP/US better than CT; stones are hypointense on MRI; the distal CBD is often hidden by gas on US.

Pancreas 🔁🔁

  • Chronic pancreatitis: calcifications, moniliform (beaded) Wirsung dilatation (CHRONIC, not acute ⚠), atrophy OR enlargement, diffuse or focal; focal enlargement mimics carcinoma.
  • Acute pancreatitis: oedema, necrosis, collections. Emergency CT: i.v. access, native phase first, lesions seen once parenchyma enhances; contrast not mandatory; the patient should NOT be rushed out "with an unequivocal diagnosis".
  • Pancreatic cancer: mass mostly in the head, poorly delineated, invades organs/vessels, nodal & liver metastases. NOT "well delineated with cystic appearance".
  • MRI for the pancreas: lesion suspected but not seen on US/CT, duct obstruction (MRCP), iodine allergy. No pancreas-specific agent; gadolinium allergy → CT.

Spleen

  • Linked to pathology: splenomegaly, cystic mass, solid space-occupying lesions, rupture after trauma. A small spleen is not necessarily pathological.

Colorectal cancer

  • Pre-operative staging: contrast-enhanced CT of the whole abdomen (± thorax); no routine head CT; US alone insufficient.
  • FDG PET-CT: staging, recurrence, pre-operative assessment, response – NOT screening (colonoscopy).
